info.title: blt API
info.description:
blt collects backup jobs and inventory from backup products (Commvault,
Rubrik) into one database. **This API is the only thing that reads or
writes that database.** Collectors never touch Postgres: they ask the API
where they left off, post what they collected, and report how the run
went. Reports and other readers use the same API.

## Signing in

Every endpoint except `/healthz` needs the API key in an `X-API-Key`
header. In these docs: **Authorize** (top right), paste the key, and the
*Try it out* buttons send it.

```
curl -H "X-API-Key: $BLT_API_KEY" \
    https://api.blt.lab.ethos.home/v1/sources/commvault/cv-toaster/last-run
```

## Conventions

- **Sources are named in the path**:
  `/v1/sources/{source type}/{source name}/...` - a CommCell is
  `/v1/sources/commvault/cv-toaster`, an RSC account
  `/v1/sources/rubrik/work`. The name is blt's own (its Prefect
  block's), not the product's. Each source type has its own endpoints
  below that, in its product's own terms.
- **Times** are ISO 8601 with a time zone (`2026-10-29T14:00:00Z`). A
  time in a request body without one is refused.
- **Lists** page with `limit` and `offset`.
- **Errors** come back as `{"detail": "..."}`: 401 for a missing or wrong
  key, 404 for an unknown source, run or job, 422 for a body or
  parameter that does not validate.
- **Writes are upserts**, keyed by the source's own ids. Posting the same
  batch twice changes nothing; a batch collected *before* what is
  already stored is ignored, so a slow run cannot roll a job back.

## Versions

Everything except `/healthz` is under `/v1`. Changes that don't break a
client (a new endpoint, field or optional parameter) are made in `/v1`
as it stands. A change that would break one goes into a `/v2` beside
it, and `/v1` stays until every collector has moved over.

The paths from before versioning (`/commcells/{name}/...`,
`/rubrik/{name}/...`) still work, for collectors on an older release.
They answer with a `Deprecation: true` header, are not listed here, and
will be removed.

## One collection run

1. `GET .../last-run` - the watermark: where the last successful run
   started. None means never collected.
2. `POST .../runs` - open a run; keep its `id`.
3. `POST .../jobs` - the jobs collected, in batches, each with the run id.
4. `POST .../runs/{run_id}/finish` - succeeded or failed. Only a
   succeeded run moves the watermark.

Commvault runs also check on jobs still active (`GET .../jobs?active=true`)
and reconcile ones the CommCell no longer knows (`PATCH .../jobs/{job_id}`).
Rubrik runs need neither: RSC reports every change, so one pass covers it.

get.summary: Where the last collection got to

The CommCell's watermark and its most recent run. An unknown
CommCell is not an error: it comes back with no watermark, which
tells a collector to start with an initial run.

post.description:
Opens a run (status `running`) and returns it; send its `id`
with each batch of jobs or objects. The CommCell is created on its
first run.

Records how the run went. A succeeded collection run (initial,
delta or full) becomes the new watermark. A succeeded inventory
run marks everything it did not list as no longer present, and
stores that day's per-instance report.

Inserts new jobs and updates known ones, keyed by Commvault's
job id. A job collected earlier than what is stored is left alone.
`written` counts the jobs actually inserted or changed.

get.description:
Jobs in job id order. The collector uses `active=true` to find
jobs to check on, and `unseen_in_run` to find ones to reconcile.

BackfillState.title: BackfillState
BackfillState.description:
How far back a CommCell's history has been collected.

`resume_from` is where the next backfill chunk should end: the oldest
point already covered, whether by a backfill or by ordinary runs.
None means nothing has been collected yet, so there is nothing to
backfill behind.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: The start of the CommCell's history has been reached.

InstanceReportRow.title: InstanceReportRow
InstanceReportRow.description:
One database instance and its most recent full backup: how many
databases the source knows on it, how many that backup took, and
which ones it missed.

`backed_up` counts the known databases whose last full is this job,
by name. `reported_backed_up` / `reported_skipped` are the backup
product's own totals for the job, kept alongside as a cross-check
rather than trusted on their own. System databases cannot be checked
by name (the source gives them no per-database job), so they are
counted in `discovered` and reported separately in `unconfirmed`.

state.description: blt's state for `status`: running, queued, waiting, pending, suspended, stopping, completed, completed_with_errors, completed_with_warnings, committed, failed, killed, no_run, missing (the CommCell no longer knows the job), or unknown.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Still going to change. A status blt does not recognise counts as active.

first_seen_at.title: First Seen At

last_collected_at.title: Last Collected At
last_collected_at.description: When this state of the job was read from the CommCell.

last_seen_run_id.title: Last Seen Run Id
last_seen_run_id.description: The last run that collected the job.

JobPatch.title: JobPatch
JobPatch.description:
A change to one already-known job - today only used to mark a job
MISSING_STATUS, since anything Commvault can still describe goes
through the batch upsert instead.

LastRun.title: LastRun
LastRun.description:
`watermark` is when the most recent *successful* collection run
(initial, delta or full - not backfill) started - the
point a delta run has to reach back to. None means nothing has ever
been collected for this CommCell, i.e. do a full run.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: The inventory run this batch belongs to.

collected_at.title: Collected At
collected_at.description: When this was read from the source.

source_key.title: Source Key
source_key.description: The source's own stable id for it, unique per kind.

parent_kind.title: Parent Kind
parent_kind.description: The parent's kind. The parent must already have been sent.

app_type.title: App Type
app_type.description: What sort of thing within its kind: "SQL Server", "File System", ...

last_backup_at.title: Last Backup At
last_backup_at.description: Its last backup, where the source reports one per object.

last_backup_job_id.title: Last Backup Job Id
last_backup_job_id.description: The job that took that backup.

last_full_job_id.title: Last Full Job Id
last_full_job_id.description: The last full backup job that included it, where the source says.

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.description: Anything else the source says about it.

ObjectIn.title: ObjectIn
ObjectIn.description:
One thing a source says exists, as that source describes it.

This is the observation layer of docs/asset-refinery.md and nothing
more: no merging, no judgement. `source_key` is the source's own
stable identifier for the thing, unique per (source, kind). A parent
is named by its own (kind, source_key) and must already have been
sent - clients before instances before databases.

present.title: Present
present.description: Listed by the latest inventory. False: it was known, and is gone.

RubrikLastRun.title: RubrikLastRun
RubrikLastRun.description:
`watermark` is when the most recent successful run started - what
a delta run reaches back to. None: never collected, do an initial
run.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: initial: first ever run, a recent window. delta: changes since the watermark, less an overlap. full: changes within the whole history limit.

lookup_seconds.title: Lookup Seconds
lookup_seconds.description: How far back the run asked for changes: everything updated after started_at minus this.

jobs_reconciled.title: Jobs Reconciled
jobs_reconciled.description: Active jobs checked on one by one.

jobs_missing.title: Jobs Missing
jobs_missing.description: Jobs marked as no longer known to the CommCell.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: initial: first ever run, active jobs plus a short recent window. delta: everything since the watermark. full: the whole history in one query. backfill: older history, a time slice at a time. inventory: what the CommCell says exists, not jobs.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When the run started. A succeeded collection run's start becomes the watermark.

lookup_seconds.title: Lookup Seconds
lookup_seconds.description: How far before started_at the run looked for jobs.

written.title: Written
written.description: Items inserted or changed. Fewer than received when some were already stored as newer.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: Rows that are stale, unprotected or empty.

ValidationReport.title: ValidationReport
ValidationReport.description:
Protection as judged from one source's own account of itself.

Today the only witness to what exists is the backup product, so this
can find what that product knows about and has not protected. It
cannot find what the product has never seen; `inventory_at` and
`sources` are here so a reader can tell how much the answer rests on.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: ok: backed up within the allowed age. stale: backed up, but longer ago. unprotected: known to the source, with no backup. empty: an instance with no databases known under it. unverified: in backup content, but the source gives no per-object backup time (SQL Server system databases). gone: the latest inventory no longer lists it.
